subject: data_science
prompt_suffix: Render this as a clean educational diagram. IMPORTANT layout constraints: - Keep the entire diagram fully contained inside the canvas. - Center the diagram and scale it down if needed. - Leave at least 15% safe margin on the left, right, top, and bottom. - No text, arrow, line, box, icon, node, label, or table cell may touch or cross the image boundaries. - Prefer a balanced landscape composition for wide diagrams. - Use a clean white background and readable Open Sans, Clear Sans, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, Segoe UI Emoji, SF Pro, sans-serif typography.

images.prompt: A diagram illustrating the difference between regression and classification. On the left, a scatter plot with a line fitting continuous data points (regression). Labels should clearly indicate "Continuous Output" for regression. On the right, a scatter plot with two distinct clusters of data points, separated by a decision boundary, each cluster labeled with a different category (classification). Labels should clearly indicate "Categorical Output" for classification.

images.prompt: A graph showing the sigmoid function (S-shaped curve). The x-axis represents the input (z, the linear combination of features), and the y-axis represents the output probability (ranging from 0 to 1). The curve should clearly show values approaching 0 for large negative inputs and approaching 1 for large positive inputs, with a steep rise around z=0, illustrating how it transforms a continuous input into a probability.

images.prompt: A simple decision tree diagram. The root node is "Outlook" with branches for "Sunny", "Overcast", "Rainy". The "Overcast" branch leads directly to a leaf node "Play". The "Sunny" branch leads to an internal node "Humidity" with branches "High" (leaf "Don't Play") and "Normal" (leaf "Play"). The "Rainy" branch leads to an internal node "Wind" with branches "Strong" (leaf "Don't Play") and "Weak" (leaf "Play").

images.prompt: A 2D scatter plot showing two distinct clusters of data points, one colored blue and one red. A solid line (the hyperplane) separates the two clusters. Two dashed lines run parallel to the solid line, one on each side, representing the margin. A few data points from each class should be highlighted, touching or near the dashed lines; these are the support vectors. Labels should clearly indicate "Hyperplane", "Margin", and "Support Vectors".
